articles.title: Paramount-Warner $81 bn merger clears key hurdle as states settle lawsuits
articles.summary:
Twelve states and Hollywood writers challenging Paramount's buyout of Warner Bros Discovery agreed to settle their lawsuits on Monday, effectively paving the way for the USD 81 billion mega merger to cross the finish line, with some new commitments from the company.
The blockbuster deal will still vastly reshape Hollywood - bringing together two of the "big five" remaining studios, key TV networks like CBS and CNN and streaming platforms HBO Max and Paramount+, as well as decades-old libraries with titles ranging from "Harry Potter" to "Top Gun."
But among terms of Monday's agreement announced by California Attorney General Rob Bonta - who led the states' case - Skydance-owned Paramount pledged to increase film production in the U.S., commit millions of dollars to a fund to support workers displaced by the merger and create new monitoring of the editorial independence of the company's news operations.
The settlement still needs a final sign-off by a judge.

articles.title: New GDP series uses GST, company data
articles.summary: New Delhi: India’s new gross domestic product series makes greater use of corporate filings, goods and services tax records and labour surveys, the statistics ministry has said in a detailed sources and methodology report for the compilation of GDP.A key change is the increased use of company-level data to estimate activity in the non-financial private corporate sector, according to the report, ‘Sources and Methods for Compilation of National Accounts Statistics’, released on Monday. India introduced the new GDP series in February, shifting the base year to 2022-23 from 2011-12.Also Read: 'Incentive scheme on the cards for critical mineral recycling'The methodology draws on corporate filings and limited liability partnership (LLP) records to improve industry classification, measure economic activity and allocate output among companies operating across multiple segments.The publication “brings together the recommendations made in the reports (already available in the public domain)” and presents, in a consolidated manner, the statistical framework and processes used to compile major macroeconomic aggregates under the new national accounts series, the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) said in a statement.Also Read: Sitharaman clarifies UPI MDR charges won't affect consumersEarlier this month, former finance secretary Subhash Garg raised concerns over the latest GDP estimates, which showed the economy growing 7.8% in the April-June quarter. He argued that the April-June 2025 nominal GDP was revised down to Rs 80 lakh crore from Rs 86 lakh crore to make growth in April-June 2026 “look better.”The methodology document, however, noted that estimates are revised as additional and more comprehensive data become available. “As additional and more comprehensive data become available, the estimates are revised to improve their accuracy and consistency,” it said.The revision policy, the ministry said, is systematic and consistent with international practices, including the recommendations of the System of National Accounts (SNA) 2008 and the International Monetary Fund’s Quarterly National Accounts Manual.“Each statistical release clearly identifies the revision status of the estimates and provides explanatory notes, describing significant changes arising from updated data or methodological improvements,” the report said. The framework also changes the estimation of the household and unincorporated sector. After evaluating different approaches, the ministry has adopted direct estimation using the Annual Survey of Unincorporated Sector Enterprises (ASUSE) and Periodic Labour Force Survey(PLFS).

articles.title: Howdy, Hanuman! Statue of Union and politics
articles.summary: TOI correspondent from Washington: Everything is supposed to be bigger in Texas, a state where cats are the size of dogs, dogs are the size of European cars, where you can fit two Germanys and 20 Belgiums - or 158 of the world's smaller countries into it.But apparently, Texas's Christian conservatives are not capacious enough to accommodate a large - very large - statue of Hanuman.Amid an uprush of "Hanumania" in India following a Hanuman Ansh movie documenting the life of the mystic Neem Karoli Baba, the largest state in contiguous America has been witnessing a blazing row over a 90-foot Hanuman statue towering over the Sri Ashtalakshmi Temple in Sugar Land outside Houston.Also Read: MAGA brown-out: For Indian Trump acolytes, citizenship comes with an asteriskConceived as a monument to strength, devotion, and unity by local Hindu groups, and officially called the Statue of the Union, the icon has become an unlikely lightning rod in Texas' increasingly heated argument over immigration, religion, identity and what counts as "American."The 90-foot, 90-ton figure was officially unveiled in August 2024 after a three-day consecration ceremony and is counted as the fourth-tallest statue in the US, behind the Birth of the New World, the Statue of Liberty, and Florida's Pegasus and Dragon.But no sooner was it installed, it attracted controversy, with members of a local church calling it a “false god" and local politicians jumping on the issue to assert that it has no place in a “Christian nation” – which, constitutionally, the US is not.Also Read: Italy’s Meloni proposes foreign student cap, school hijab ban amid far-right challengeSince then, arguments for and against the statue have surfaced frequently in an increasingly toxic atmosphere in a once-capacious state that has seen a large influx of Indian-origin residents, particularly in and around Dallas and Houston.Indian-American community leaders maintain that the statue is not an assertion that Texas has suddenly become India, but rather that Hindu Americans are part of Texas."There's nothing that's un-American about it," says Dr Vijay Sreenarasimhaiah, a former temple board member, arguing that the statue's message of bringing people together reflected constitutional values.Temple members also say the structure is fully legal and they followed all due permitting processes.Engineers designed the structure to withstand hurricane-force winds exceeding 180 mph that the area is sometimes subjected to.The statue was constructed by traditional Indian sthapatis, or temple sculptors, shipped to Texas in pieces and assembled on site. The project cost about $8 million and was financed through donations from Hindus in Houston and elsewhere in the US.(The idea for the statue came from Sri Chinna Jeeyar Swami, the Indian spiritual leader who also conceived Hyderabad's Statue of Equality. He envisioned Hanuman as a “builder of bridges" and a symbol of unity, and named it the Statue of Union because Hanuman, in the Ramayana, helps reunite Rama and Sita.)The irony is that Hanuman is hardly a recent immigrant to America. At the Mount Madonna Centre in California, the Sankat Mochan Hanuman Temple grew out of the devotion of American followers of Neem Karoli Baba, venerated by a legion of celebrities in Silicon Valley, Hollywood, and Bollywood - from the late Steve Jobs and Mark Zuckerberg to Julia Roberts and Virat Kohli.After Baba's death in 1973, American devotees commissioned a Hanuman murti; the temple was consecrated in 2003.In New Mexico, the Neem Karoli Baba Ashram likewise traces its Hanuman devotion to American followers from the late 1970s.In Texas itself, the Karya Siddhi Hanuman temple in Frisco developed from a satsang group formed in 1999; its stone shrine was carved in Bengaluru and assembled by a team of 29 sculptors in 2015.And the cultural reach of Hanuman extends far beyond Hindu immigrants. Barack Obama, hardly the image of an Indian religious traditionalist, disclosed in a 2016 interview that among the small objects he carried in his pocket as personal reminders and good-luck charms was a miniature Hanuman figurine given to him by a woman.The National Archives confirms the existence of a Hanuman figurine in the Obama presidential collection.The backlash, however, has migrated from theology into politics amid increasing race-baiting and xenophobia in the MAGA universe. In February this year, Carlos Turcios, a Texas conservative activist, released a social-media video of the statue, describing it as evidence that "third world aliens" were taking over Texas and America.And last month, conservative commentator Kaylee Campbell pushed ahead with the fear-mongering with the question: "How is anyone supposed to take Texas seriously when we have a 90-foot 'monkey god' statue?"Texas politicians themselves have sent mixed signals. Governor Greg Abbott, while not specifically commenting on the statue, has publicly courted Texas' Indian-American community, saying at a Diwali celebration, “As long as I am governor of this great state, Texas will be a land for the Indian community." But the fireworks just won't stop.

articles.summary: Paramount Skydance has settled with California and 11 other states that sued to block its $110 billion acquisition of Warner Bros Discovery, a source familiar with the matter said on Monday, clearing one of the last hurdles to a deal that would reshape Hollywood.The settlement includes the creation of independent editorial boards for CNN and CBS, the source said, a move aimed at safeguarding the independence of their news operations under the combined company.Also Read: Paramount, states could settle Warner Bros. $110 billion deal challenge this weekend, sources sayIt also includes a $30 million penalty per film for any shortfall against Paramount's pledge to release 30 movies annually, the source said.Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros Discovery did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment on the settlement.The settlement would remove a major obstacle to closing one of the largest media mergers in history, letting Paramount move forward with a combination that will unite two of Hollywood's biggest film studios, two major streaming services and two of the largest cable-news operations under a single owner.Reuters first reported on Friday that Paramount and the states could settle as soon as the weekend, with independent content monitoring of CNN and a commitment on the number of theatrical releases among the terms under discussion.Also Read: EU approves Paramount's $81 billion Warner Bros. mega merger deal with conditionsThe Wall Street Journal reported on Sunday that the two sides had discussed a range of concessions, including a $1.5 billion investment in production in the state, a commitment not to sell either studio lot, and potential penalties if Paramount fails to honor a pledge to produce 30 movies a year after the merger.Other measures under consideration include selling some cable channels and creating a board to help ensure CNN retains editorial independence, WSJ had reported.While Trump administration regulators cleared the deal, a coalition of 12 state attorneys general, led by California's Rob Bonta, sued in July to block the merger, arguing it would reduce competition and create a media behemoth with the power to raise prices in movies and television.A settlement will help Paramount avoid a $7 million daily fee it owes Warner Bros shareholders for each day the deal does not close past September 30.Antitrust regulators in other jurisdictions globally, including the European Union and Britain, have already cleared the acquisition.

articles.title: Forex inflows rise to USD 143.6 billion
articles.summary: Foreign exchange inflows under the Reserve Bank of India's special USD-INR forex swap facility have risen to USD 143.60 billion, with Foreign Currency Non-Resident (Bank) or FCNR(B) deposits increasing by about USD 5.75 billion from the provisional figure reported earlier this month.According to an RBI release issued on Monday, FCNR(B) deposits mobilised till August 31 stood at USD 132.98 billion, compared with the provisional USD 127.226 billion reported earlier, an increase of USD 5.754 billion.The latest data showed that Overseas Foreign Currency Borrowings (OFCBs) contributed USD 5.32 billion, while External Commercial Borrowings (ECBs) accounted for USD 5.296 billion. The increase was driven mainly by the upward revision in FCNR(B) deposits and higher ECB inflows.The central bank had introduced the special USD-INR forex swap facility on June 8, covering inflows through FCNR(B) deposits, ECBs and OFCBs."RBI had introduced a special USD-INR Forex Swap facility covering FCNR(B) deposits, ECB and OFCB inflows on June 08, 2026," the release said.The window for FCNR(B) deposits remained open until August 31, while the facility for ECBs and OFCBs will remain available until December 31, 2026, the RBI said.The central bank clarified that the USD 132.98 billion FCNR(B) figure represents deposits mobilised up to August 31.

articles.title: Namibian cheetah 'Gaurav' dies in Kuno
articles.summary: A 10-year-old Namibian cheetah, Gaurav, died at Madhya Pradesh's Kuno National Park on Monday evening while undergoing treatment, an official said.Gaurav had been rescued from the wild on September 12 after officials noticed that the cheetah appeared weak and dull. He was subsequently brought in for medical assessment and treatment.Gaurav was found weak and severely dehydratedAccording to the field director of the cheetah project, Gaurav was found to be in a significantly weakened condition when he was examined."On examination, he was found to be markedly weak, with visible muscle wasting and severe dehydration. Immediate systemic and supportive treatment was provided, following which he was shifted to Palpur and kept in a Quarantine Boma (QB) for close observation and further management," the field director said.Based on the initial clinical examination, officials suspected that Gaurav could have been suffering from an underlying chronic condition.Namibian cheetah's condition deterioratedDespite receiving continued treatment and supportive care, Gaurav's condition worsened."Despite continued treatment and supportive care, his condition deteriorated, and he died at around 4 pm on Monday," the field director said.Officials have not yet determined the exact cause of death.Postmortem to establish cause of deathThe official said the precise cause will be established after a postmortem examination and analysis of samples collected following Gaurav's death."Further details will be available once the reports are received," the official said.The findings are expected to provide more information about the health condition that may have contributed to the cheetah's deterioration.Kuno National Park now has 51 cheetahsFollowing Gaurav's death, Kuno National Park has 51 cheetahs, including 36 that were born in India, according to the official.Of the 51 cheetahs at Kuno, 16 are currently ranging freely in the wild.The official added that four cheetahs are currently housed at Gandhi Sagar Sanctuary. This takes India's total cheetah population to 55.Gaurav's death comes as India's cheetah reintroduction programme continues to expand across designated habitats, with officials monitoring the health and movement of the animals brought into the country as well as those born in India.Inputs from PTI
